extDescription.message: Hebrew (and other right-to-left) mail the right way round: each paragraph you write takes its direction from its words, Ctrl + right/left Shift switch it by hand, and received Hebrew messages are shown right-to-left.

composeActionTitle.message: Lossmol: switch the paragraph's direction (Ctrl + right Shift: right-to-left, Ctrl + left Shift: left-to-right)

composeStateRtl.message: This paragraph runs right to left. Click to make it left to right.

composeStateLtr.message: This paragraph runs left to right. Click to make it right to left.

displayActionTitle.message: Lossmol: show this message as it arrived, or fixed

menuDisplayThisOriginal.message: Show this message as it arrived

displayStateFixed.message: Lossmol re-aligned $COUNT$ paragraphs here. Click to see the message as it arrived.

displayStateNone.message: Lossmol: this message is shown as it arrived; nothing to re-align.

displayStateOff.message: Lossmol is off for this message: shown as it arrived. Click to re-align.

optionsComposeAuto.message: Each paragraph takes its direction from its words as I type (mostly Hebrew: right-to-left)

optionsComposeShortcuts.message: By hand, at any time: the toolbar button switches the paragraph; Ctrl + right Shift makes it right-to-left and Ctrl + left Shift left-to-right; the whole message is in the editor's right-click menu.

optionsSendHtml.message: Send as HTML when a paragraph has a direction. Otherwise Thunderbird's "Automatic" sending format may send plain text, and the direction is lost on the way.

optionsDisplayFix.message: Show received messages paragraph by paragraph in the direction of their words, even when they arrived left-aligned

optionsNote.message: Changes apply to windows opened from now on; a message already open follows the reading setting right away.
